extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, petitioners, and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) participating in USPTO post-grant/inter partes/covered-business-method review proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing institution, scope, motions to amend, estoppel, evidence, timing, joinder, and related practice in AIA post-grant, inter partes, and covered business method patent review proceedings before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of institution decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the rules, the Board may authorize the review to proceed on all or some of the challenged claims and on all or some of the grounds of unpatentability asserted for each claim. (§§ 42.108(a) and 42.208(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision to institute can be claim-by-claim and ground-by-ground; the Board has discretion to limit proceedings to particular claims/grounds to streamline issues for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory threshold for instituting review
rubrics_metrics.description: Review will not be instituted unless the Board decides that the petition supporting the ground would demonstrate that there is a reasonable likelihood (for inter partes proceedings), or more likely than not (for post-grant proceedings), that at least one of the claims is unpatentable. (35 U.S.C. 314(a) and 324(a))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'reasonable likelihood' is a lower threshold than 'more likely than not.' Whether the petitioner meets the threshold must be considered case-by-case. The rules adopt the statutory thresholds rather than further defining them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of timeliness and complexity in institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may take into account whether the review could be timely completed and may decline to institute where it could not complete the proceeding timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where Board may decline: petitions seeking review of several hundred claims based on a thousand references, or where determination would require dozens of depositions of non-party witnesses in foreign countries requiring compelled testimony. The AIA requires consideration of the integrity of the patent system, efficient administration, and ability to complete proceedings timely (35 U.S.C. 316(b), 326(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of challenged claims in the petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to institute a review must identify each claim challenged. (35 U.S.C. 312(a)(3), 322(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only claims identified and for which review is instituted are subject to estoppel; petition must specify claim-level challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim-by-claim institution and estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition is required to identify the claims being challenged, and only those claims upon which review is instituted are subject to estoppel. Estoppel under 35 U.S.C. 315(e) and 325(e) applies on a claim-by-claim basis for claims resulting in a final written decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limiting review to only those claims that meet the threshold streamlines issues and reduces burden on patent owner; it prevents forcing responses to non-meritorious grounds that fail the initial thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of a ground is a final Board decision (and non-reviewability of institution determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may deny a ground at any time prior to institution before or after receiving any patent owner preliminary response. Denial of a ground is a final Board decision and thus is subject to request for reconsideration at that time. (§ 42.71(c)(2)) The decision of the Director on whether to institute review on any ground is not reviewable. (35 U.S.C. 314(d), 324(e))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although denial of a ground is final for that ground, institution determinations by the Director are not subject to judicial review; the Board may deny individual grounds even in a decision to institute on other grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of institution and sufficiency of reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Under § 42.4(a) and 35 U.S.C. 314(c)/324(d), the Notice is required to inform the parties in writing of the Director’s determination of whether to institute a proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will provide sufficient notice to the parties in its decision to institute a trial; commenters' requests for an explicit written statement 'stating each reason for denial' were addressed by relying on the statutory Notice requirement rather than imposing additional formulaic language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of patent owner preliminary response
rubrics_metrics.description: For post-grant review, the patent owner may set forth 'reasons' why no review should be instituted based upon failure of the petition to meet requirements; the Board will take into account a patent owner’s preliminary response where such a response is filed. (§ 42.208(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director nonetheless may deny a petition prior to receiving a preliminary response if the petition fails to set forth sufficient grounds; the petition must itself set forth sufficient grounds to justify institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel or unsettled legal question basis for post-grant review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may institute a proceeding where the petition raises a novel or unsettled legal question that is important to other patents or patent applications. (35 U.S.C. 324(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether a petition raises such a novel or unsettled legal question important to others will be decided case-by-case; there's no artificial restriction on instituting review on that basis, but the scope of review is limited to the statutory grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing timelines for institution decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may file a request for rehearing of a decision not to institute a review within thirty days of the entry of the decision. A petitioner may request a rehearing of a decision to institute a review that denies a ground of unpatentability within fourteen days. (Pursuant to § 42.71)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing timeframes differ depending on whether the decision is not to institute (30 days) or to institute with denial of a ground (14 days), reflecting nonfinal vs. final aspects of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of non-institution on final written decision and estoppel
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board’s determination not to institute an inter partes review, post-grant review, or covered business method patent review is not a final written decision within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 318(a)/328(a), and thereby does not trigger estoppel provisions under 35 U.S.C. 315(e)/325(e). However, pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 314(d) and 324(e), a decision not to institute a trial is 'final and nonappealable' for purposes of judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not instituting does not create estoppel in later proceedings, but parties generally cannot seek judicial review of the Director's institution decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel exception for settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel shall not apply to a petitioner, or to the real party-in-interest or privy of the petitioner who has settled under 35 U.S.C. 317 or 327. If a joint request of petitioner and patent owner under 317(a) or 327(a) is filed before the Office enters the final written decision, the review is terminated with respect to the petitioner and no estoppel will attach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlement and timely joint request terminate review for that petitioner and avoid estoppel attaching to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner may submit evidence with petition (limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may include evidence (except new testimony evidence beyond that which is already of record) in connection with the petition process, which the Office will take into account. (§§ 42.107(a) & (c), 42.207(a) & (c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will consider such evidence and may consider whether to authorize a motion to dismiss based on the facts. Limitations apply to new testimonial evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default time period for filing patent owner response (3 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no time for filing a patent owner response to a petition is provided in a Board order, the default date for filing a patent owner response is three months from the date the review was instituted. (Sections 42.120(b) and 42.220(b))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rule extended the default from two to three months in response to comments; Board orders can set different deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for first motion to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless a due date is provided in a Board order, a motion to amend must be filed no later than the filing of a patent owner response. (§§ 42.121(a)(1) and 42.221(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first motion to amend does not require Board authorization but does require the patent owner to 'confer with the Board' (e.g., a conference call to identify intent and number/scope of substitute claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional motions to amend require good cause or settlement
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional motion to amend may be authorized when there is a good cause showing or a joint request of the petitioner and patent owner to materially advance a settlement. (§§ 42.121(c) and 42.221(c))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will authorize further motions only on good cause or settlement grounds to avoid delay and inefficiency; failure to meet authorization requirements may result in denial of the additional motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of one substitute claim per challenged claim
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a presumption that only one substitute claim per challenged claim is reasonable, expressly in §§ 42.121(a) and 42.221(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may rebut the presumption by demonstration of need; presenting more claims than necessary likely causes delay/complexity and may require excess claim fees (35 U.S.C. 41(a)(2); amounts in § 42.15(e),(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment substantive restrictions (no new matter, no enlargement, must respond to grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motions to amend (including the first motion) may be denied where the amendment does not respond to a ground of unpatentability, seeks to enlarge the scope of the claims, or introduces new matter. Failure to comply with any requirement may result in denial. (§§ 42.121, 42.221)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments should narrow claims and be responsive to grounds of unpatentability; amendments not meeting these requirements will be denied rather than entered and substantively rejected later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and support requirements for proposed substitute claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must clearly state 'original,' 'cancelled,' 'replaced by proposed substitute,' or 'proposed substitute for original claim X' and the motion must clearly describe the changes. Amendments should clearly state where the specification and any drawings disclose all the limitations in the proposed substitute claims and the patentably distinct features. (§ Part II, Item G of the Patent Trial Practice Guide referenced)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable substitute claim example: adds a patentably distinct feature to respond to a ground without adding new matter or enlarging scope. Conforming amendments may be presented. This aids the Board in assessing whether the amendment narrows claims and responds to grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for presenting number/need for substitute claims (conference call and scheduling order)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board will enter a Scheduling Order concurrently with the decision to institute the review. An initial conference call will be held about one month from the date of institution to discuss intended motions and determine if scheduling adjustments are needed; during the call the patent owner identifies the number of substitute claims intended and reasons why more than one per claim is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may indicate whether the number of substitute claims seems reasonable based on reasons given. Patent owner is not required to identify a fully developed claim set at the call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for excess/new claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment adds more than one substitute claim per claim, the patent owner may be required to pay excess claims fees. The Office provided amounts in § 42.15(e) and (f) (subject to later section 10 rulemaking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: changes in number of independent claims may trigger payment of excess claim fees with the motion to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oppositions and replies to motions to amend; new evidence in opposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 42.23 provides for oppositions and replies. A petitioner will be afforded an opportunity to respond fully to an amendment. Petitioners may supplement evidence submitted with their petition to respond to new issues arising from proposed substitute claims, including new expert declarations directed to the proposed substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling Orders generally set times for oppositions and replies. Oppositions and replies must comply with motion content requirements; replies may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding opposition. A reply that raises a new issue or belatedly presents evidence will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments are not permitted in the patent owner’s preliminary response
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend the patent is not provided for until after the institution of a review. (35 U.S.C. 316(d)(1) and 326(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner may discuss scope of intended substitute claims during the conference call, but formal claim amendments require filing a motion to amend after institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of English translations for non-English disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 42.63(b) requires an English language translation of any non-English language document relied upon by a party, and an affidavit attesting to the accuracy of the translation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an earlier-filed disclosure cited in an amendment is not in English, a certified translation must be submitted with the amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative/contingent claim sets allowed if reasonable total number
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternative claim sets or contingent amendments may be permitted if the total number of substitute claims is reasonable. (§§ 42.121(a)(3) and 42.221(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonableness assessed in context; patent owner should justify need during conference call and in motion to amend.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scheduling order default timing for petitioner replies and oppositions
rubrics_metrics.description: The default Scheduling Order generally will provide the petitioner with three months for discovery and for filing a petitioner’s reply to the patent owner’s response and any opposition to the motion to amend; parties may request adjustments at the initial conference call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheduling Order sets due dates taking into account complexity, while ensuring trial completion within one year of institution (with possible six-month extension for good cause).

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinder request timing and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Joinder may be requested by filing a motion within one month of the date that the trial is instituted. When determining whether to grant joinder, the Office will consider particular facts including how consolidation impacts the Office’s ability to complete reviews timely. (§§ 42.122 and 42.222 modified to provide time period)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Replacement of a consenting petitioner is not provided by statute; a petitioner may settle and enter a joint request to terminate, which affects estoppel as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation counting toward instituted proceeding limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where multiple instituted proceedings are consolidated, each proceeding would be counted towards any limit that might be established as each is a separately instituted proceeding that is thereafter consolidated into a single proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation does not reduce the count of instituted proceedings for any statutory or regulatory limit; each instituted proceeding remains counted.
